findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was a fork observed to be in the front handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The fork was removed from the handwashing sink and it was discussed to only use the handwashing sink for handwashing. Ensure that all staff are educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The mini fridge that holds sauces is observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. The PIC stated that most of the sauces had been made and put in the cooler about an hour prior to the inspection. These sauces were moved to another cooler, while the rest of the sauces were voluntarily discarded (a bottle of honey mustard and a bottle of Western dressing.) The facility has enough cold holding without the use of this mini fridge. The PIC stated that they will be attempting to get a new one. Ensure that if a new mini fridge is obtained that it is properly cold holding at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The gasket of the left door of the main preparation cooler is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT- There was no one present in the facility that has completed their allergen awareness training. All Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM) must also complete training in basic allergen awareness principles. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility that has their Allergen Awareness Training certificate during all hours of operation and food preparation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the large cooler in the back kitchen area had raw bacon on the top shelf above cheese, potatoes, and other ready-to-eat food items. The PIC was notified, and the raw bacon was moved to the bottom shelf, where it was below these foods. Ensure that raw meats are stored below READY TO EAT foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several sauces made in house that were still in the coolers past their date-marking, including a honey mustard dressing that was made in house that should have been discarded 30 March 2026. The PIC and staff were notified, and the out-of-date sauces were voluntarily discarded. It is important that TCS foods, especially ones that are prepared “in house” in an establishment, are discarded after 7 days, with day 1 being the date of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is in need of repair:
(1) The gasket of the left door of the prep cooler in the front kitchen is in disrepair.
(2) The large standing cooler in the back had a dish rag tied around a dripping hose. According to the PIC, this was placed there by the plumber.
The PIC was notified of the issues, and will work on getting them repaired by the next routine inspection.
Ensure that equipment is maintained in good working order that prevents contamination and loss of temperature control.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following surfaces in need of cleaning:
(1) the shelving in the back kitchen standing cooler - there was an accumulation of soil residue on the shelves.
(2) the right side of the front kitchen prep cooler - there was significant accumulation of soil residue - the prep cooler should be moved for cleaning.
The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean these surfaces before the next routine inspection.
It is important that nonfood-contact surfaces be cleaned frequently to prevent the build up of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
(1st Repeat) Inspectors observed that no one present in the facility at the start of the inspection has completed the allergen awareness training. All Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM) must also complete training in basic allergen awareness principles. Ensure that sufficient employees have the allergen certificate by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the prep cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The hanging internal thermometer was reading at about 55F. The following internal temperatures were recorded: jalapeños 53F, chicken 51F, turkey 50F, ham 53F, burger patty 49F, chorizo 49F, parmesan cheese 52F, monterey jack cheese 55F, southwest sauce 56F, spicy mayo 58F, sour cream cups 58F, and salsa cups 53F. Non-temperature control for safety (TCS) foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. onions, jalapeños, pickles, various non-dairy based sauce, strawberries, corn mix, avocados). Some of the TCS foods were put inside the cooler at 8:30 am and other TCS foods has been inside the cooler since last night. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since last night and were voluntarily discarded: turkey, ham, feta cheese, parmesan cheese, burger patties, dairy bases sauces (southwest, spicy mayo, and mayo), sour cream cups, and salsa cups. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since 8:30 am and were put under time-as-control (TAC) to be discarded at 12:30 pm: lettuce, cut tomato, all cheeses, chicken, and chorizo. The PIC wrote down and posted above the prep cooler the foods that must be discarded and the time they will be discarded. The PIC also mentioned that they are not busy today and will most likely close at 12:30 pm. The PIC spoke with Koady Hawkins who stated they will be scheduling service for the cooler. They will be putting small amounts of TCS foods that can be used within four hours inside the prep cooler until it is serviced. They were reminded that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler without TAC until it is cold holding foods at 41F or below. For information about the cooler, see violation #33.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed the prep cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. For information about the food, see violation #22. The inspector will follow-up to check that the cooler is functioning correctly on 7/14/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the storage room produce refrigerator (closest to the entrance door) has an accumulation of food residue on the inside bottom. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the refrigerator bottom is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee operate the cash register and then put on gloves to cook an omelet without hand washing inbetween. The inspector educated that all employees must wash hands before donning gloves for food preparation. The PIC will be reminding employees about proper glove use and hand washing procedures. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on a counter top. The inspector educated about proper storage and the wiping cloth was placed into sanitizer solution during the inspection. Wet in-use wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer between uses. They can never sit out on counters once wet. At the end of the day all used wiping cloths must be laundered. Ensure that wet in-use wiping cloths are always stored correctly and laundered daily. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the handle of the prep cooler is in disrepair. The PIC stated they have the parts to fix the handle but they haven’t serviced it yet. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. The handle must be repaired by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the employee working did not have their food handler training. All food handlers, other than those with the certified food protection manager (CFPM) certificate, must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all required employees obtain the food handler training by the next routine inspection 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness training expired on 06/08/2024. There must be someone present at the facility who has completed the allergen awareness training during all hours of operation. Ensure that all CFPM’s have the allergen awareness training completed by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the back handwashing sink was blocked with dish cleaning supplies. The PIC moved the cleaning supplies out of the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks are accessible at all times. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed eggs being stored on the top shelf of a cooler over ready-to-eat foods (including, but not limited too, cut vegetables). Ensure that eggs are stored below ready-to-eat foods. Foods must be stored according to their correct storage order to prevent cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
